statement: The CCDR estimates about 463 km2 of urban area is at high risk of flooding from rivers, rain and sea-level rise; many affected urban residents live in unplanned settlements without adequate drainage.
compact_statement: The CCDR estimates about 463 km2 of urban area is at high risk of flooding from rivers, rain and sea-level rise; many affected urban residents live in unplanned settlements without adequate drainage.
uncertainty: Modeled high-risk area is not a count of people or observed flood damage.

statement: The CCDR estimates 27.7 percent of Tanzania's population and 29.4 percent of its vulnerable population are exposed to at least one climate risk.
compact_statement: The CCDR estimates 27.7 percent of Tanzania's population and 29.4 percent of its vulnerable population are exposed to at least one climate risk.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 8, population exposure to climate risks

uncertainty: The summary aggregates exposure to at least one risk and does not disaggregate by hazard here.

statement: The CCDR says about 70 percent of Tanzania's population depends on agriculture, many as poor smallholder farmers, and is poorly positioned to manage repeated or simultaneous climate shocks.
compact_statement: The CCDR says about 70 percent of Tanzania's population depends on agriculture, many as poor smallholder farmers, and is poorly positioned to manage repeated or simultaneous climate shocks.
uncertainty: This is the report's national characterization; the passage does not give a farmer-level impact estimate.

statement: The NDC reports average maximum temperatures rose over 1 degree C in 1961-2013 and drying occurred in northeastern and much of southern Tanzania during 1981-2016, affecting agriculture, water and energy.
compact_statement: The NDC reports average maximum temperatures rose over 1 degree C in 1961-2013 and drying occurred in northeastern and much of southern Tanzania during 1981-2016, affecting agriculture, water and energy.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 17, observed temperature and drying trends

uncertainty: The NDC summarizes prior national-communication trend analyses through 2016.

statement: NDC projects 0.8-1.8 degrees C warming by the 2040s and 1.6-5.0 degrees C by 2090; dry-season rainfall may decline, wet-season rainfall rise, with southern decline and Lake Victoria-area increase by 2030.
compact_statement: NDC projects 0.8-1.8 degrees C warming by the 2040s and 1.6-5.0 degrees C by 2090; dry-season rainfall may decline, wet-season rainfall rise, with southern decline and Lake Victoria-area increase by 2030.
scenario: The inspected summary does not specify it.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 18, Future Climate for Africa projections

uncertainty: Projections cite Future Climate for Africa (2017); rainfall patterns vary by season and region.

statement: The NDC sets a target to raise access to clean, safe water from 2015 baselines of 86 percent in urban areas and 67.7 percent in rural areas to 100 percent by 2030.
compact_statement: The NDC sets a target to raise access to clean, safe water from 2015 baselines of 86 percent in urban areas and 67.7 percent in rural areas to 100 percent by 2030.
uncertainty: This is an NDC target; it does not demonstrate achieved 2030 coverage.

statement: Source dated 2025-03 reports: The audit's cited July 2024 report says the 2023 Hanang mudslide affected 261 houses, destroyed 95, damaged 754.875 acres of farmland and disrupted 742 businesses.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-03 reports: The audit's cited July 2024 report says the 2023 Hanang mudslide affected 261 houses, destroyed 95, damaged 754.875 acres of farmland and disrupted 742 businesses.

source_refs.locator: Printed p. 59, section 3.4.2, citing the July 2024 Hanang post-landslide restoration report.

uncertainty: Event-specific totals are relayed from a district restoration report; this figure set does not establish climate attribution.

statement: Source dated 2025-03 reports: In Kilosa, auditors observed a Standard Gauge Railway stormwater culvert without a continuous downstream channel; accumulated floodwater affected neighboring areas.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-03 reports: In Kilosa, auditors observed a Standard Gauge Railway stormwater culvert without a continuous downstream channel; accumulated floodwater affected neighboring areas.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 58-63, sections 3.4.1-3.4.2 and photos 3.3(e)-(f), Kilosa site observation.

uncertainty: September 2024 site observation; the audit attributes this instance to drainage obstruction, not climate change.

statement: Source dated 2025-03 reports: In 2024, none of five visited councils had demarcated or protected identified flood-prone areas; the audit tables show no disaster-coordination allocations in Kinondoni, Hanang, Mbeya or Kilosa, unlike Rufiji.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-03 reports: In 2024, none of five visited councils had demarcated or protected identified flood-prone areas; the audit tables show no disaster-coordination allocations in Kinondoni, Hanang, Mbeya or Kilosa, unlike Rufiji.
institutions: Prime Minister's Office Disaster Management Division
President's Office Regional Administration and Local Government

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 37-38 and 53-54, sections 3.3.1 and 3.3.7; tables 3.2 and 3.6.

uncertainty: Selected 2024 audit councils, not national prevalence; narrative/table sample counts differ. Missing budgets/demarcation are institutional preparedness gaps, not FCV constraints.

statement: The ministry's 2024 sector report describes above-average Rufiji rainfall and high Great Ruaha flow at Msembe during the 2023–2024 season.
compact_statement: The ministry's 2024 sector report describes above-average Rufiji rainfall and high Great Ruaha flow at Msembe during the 2023–2024 season.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 12-14, sections 3.1.1.1 and 3.1.1.3, Rufiji Basin rainfall and river-flow discussion.

uncertainty: Basin/station observations, not national household loss or anthropogenic attribution; percentage-above versus percentage-of-average is not silently converted.

statement: Source dated 2025-03 reports: The Ministry assigns local water allocation to Water User Associations and rural-scheme operation to community water organizations; it reports staff, data, storage and financing gaps in 2024.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025-03 reports: The Ministry assigns local water allocation to Water User Associations and rural-scheme operation to community water organizations; it reports staff, data, storage and financing gaps in 2024.

source_refs.locator: Printed pp. 2-3 and 73-74, institutional roles and chapter 4 constraints.

uncertainty: The report lists sector-wide constraints and does not assess the capacity or service performance of named local associations.

statement: Source dated 2021 reports: A 2021 cross-sectional study of 120 respondents in selected Kilosa wards and villages reports farmer-pastoralist conflict over land, water and pasture and attributes resource scarcity partly to climate variability.
compact_statement: Source dated 2021 reports: A 2021 cross-sectional study of 120 respondents in selected Kilosa wards and villages reports farmer-pastoralist conflict over land, water and pasture and attributes resource scarcity partly to climate variability.

source_refs.locator: Sokoine University repository abstract, methods and findings paragraphs.

uncertainty: Author abstract reports perceived/resource-related association in selected Kilosa sites; full text, ward names and causal identification unavailable.

statement: Source dated 2025 reports: A 2025 mixed-methods study across Monduli and Longido reports that responsiveness, accountability, transparency and stakeholder participation significantly influenced local adaptation implementation, with participation strongest.
compact_statement: Source dated 2025 reports: A 2025 mixed-methods study across Monduli and Longido reports that responsiveness, accountability, transparency and stakeholder participation significantly influenced local adaptation implementation, with participation strongest.

source_refs.locator: Repository abstract, methods and results paragraphs.

uncertainty: Abstract-only reported governance associations, not causal effects or district-specific outcome estimates.

statement: Source dated 2026-08-24 reports: The brief cites estimates that preparedness receives about 25% of the disaster-management budget, while the Water Ministry assigns about 6% to water-resource management versus 75% to water supply.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-08-24 reports: The brief cites estimates that preparedness receives about 25% of the disaster-management budget, while the Water Ministry assigns about 6% to water-resource management versus 75% to water supply.
institutions: Prime Minister's Office Disaster Management Department

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 2, national adaptation budgeting context and cited preparedness budget shares.

uncertainty: Budget shares are cited in the brief from 2023-2025 sources; they are not the brief's own fiscal audit.

statement: Source dated 2026-08-24 reports: The 43-interview study identifies reactive-response norms, budget ceilings, institutional silos, weak coordination authority and generic monitoring as mutually reinforcing reasons flood and drought preparedness is underfunded.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-08-24 reports: The 43-interview study identifies reactive-response norms, budget ceilings, institutional silos, weak coordination authority and generic monitoring as mutually reinforcing reasons flood and drought preparedness is underfunded.
institutions: Prime Minister's Office Disaster Management Department

source_refs.locator: PDF pp. 3-5, results of the 2025 interview and budget-cycle analysis.

uncertainty: Qualitative purposive interview findings concern national budget processes, not local flood- or drought-loss outcomes.

statement: Source dated 2026-08-24 reports: The brief recommends preparedness rules in budget guidelines, costed and coordinated ministry plans, and transparent tracking of planned and actual preparedness spending.
compact_statement: Source dated 2026-08-24 reports: The brief recommends preparedness rules in budget guidelines, costed and coordinated ministry plans, and transparent tracking of planned and actual preparedness spending.

source_refs.locator: PDF p. 5 and summary, proposed budget-cycle leverage points.

uncertainty: These are recommendations, not reported policy changes or completed preparedness investments.

statement: Source dated not stated reports: The Dodoma project describes its Chamwino and Mpwapwa target communities as groundwater-dependent; unreliable rainfall affects crops and livestock and is associated with drought, flooding, erosion and limited recharge.
compact_statement: Source dated not stated reports: The Dodoma project describes its Chamwino and Mpwapwa target communities as groundwater-dependent; unreliable rainfall affects crops and livestock and is associated with drought, flooding, erosion and limited recharge.

source_refs.locator: IKI project page, initial situation and project-area description.

uncertainty: The grant-programme description is regional and project-framed; it does not provide district-level hazard measurements.

statement: Source dated not stated reports: The completed project reports community-led plans adopted by Chamwino and Mpwapwa councils, 25 adaptation actions added to 2024/25 plans and budgets, and TZS 500 million approved for implementation.
compact_statement: Source dated not stated reports: The completed project reports community-led plans adopted by Chamwino and Mpwapwa councils, 25 adaptation actions added to 2024/25 plans and budgets, and TZS 500 million approved for implementation.

source_refs.locator: IKI project page, completed-project status and key achievements.

uncertainty: Reported council adoption and approved TZS500million allocation, not verified disbursement or evaluated losses prevented.
